newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban says it holds ex-governor Khan.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban says it holds ex-governor Khan.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia said on Thursday it was now holding the captured former Herat province governor Ismail Khan, an important figure in an opposition alliance fighting it.

Ismail, who was reported captured on Monday in the northwestern province of Faryab in a mutiny by an alliance general, is in poor health and was shifted to the southern city of Kandahar on Wednesday night, the Taleban-controlled Kabul radio said.

Earlier, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service quoted Taleban sources as saying Ismail was handed over on Wednesday night by the forces of General Abdul Malik, who mutinied on Monday against anti-Talbean northern warlord General Abdul Rashid Dostum.

Ismail, a trusted lieutenant of ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani, had fled to Iran after being ousted from Herat by the Taleban in September 1995. But he had been fighting them in northwest Afghanistan in recent months.
Rabbani's forces forged an alliance with Dostum after being ousted from Kabul by the Taleban in September last year.
